item.title: China-Laos "Peace Train-2026" joint exercise wraps up
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
By Zhou Na, Liu Xiaowei, Chi Xuedong, Zhang Tianyu, Yang Chao, Yin Chuandong, Tan Yuzhou and Tan Youming VIENTIANE, Sept. 15 -- The China-Laos "Peace Train-2026" joint humanitarian medical rescue exercise concluded in Vientiane, Laos, on September 14, 2026, after completing all scheduled training activities. Leaders from both sides presented representatives of the participating troops with the "Third-Class Medal of Valor" and the "Friendship Medal" conferred by the Lao Ministry of National Defense, as well as "Certificates of Participation" issued by the medical service commanders of the two militaries. Chinese representatives also donated medical supplies, including pharmaceuticals, to the Lao People's Army. After the exercise, the "Peace Train" medical team will provide specialized diagnosis and treatment, surgery demonstrations, physical examinations, academic lectures, and other medical services in Vientiane, Pakse in Champasak Province, and other locations. (Video Editor: Lin Congyi)

item.title: Xi urges Chinese police to remain committed to serving people with responsibility, dedication
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
BEIJING, Sept. 15 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has called on the country's police officers to remain committed to serving the people, be loyal guardians of the Party and the people, and demonstrate a strong sense of responsibility and dedication. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a reply letter to a primary-level police force from Zhangzhou, east China's Fujian Province. In his letter to the "Zhangzhou 110" police unit, Xi lauded its police officers for their dedication and hard work at the grassroots level in serving the public and maintaining social stability for the people. He emphasized that the police bear the important responsibility of safeguarding the people's well-being and the country's peace, calling on Chinese police to uphold fine traditions, devote themselves to wholeheartedly addressing the needs and concerns of the people, and work diligently to protect the safety of the public. The "Zhangzhou 110" unit is one of the exemplary primary-level units within China's police forces. Since 1990, it has pioneered and continuously improved a rapid response mechanism tied to the 110 police emergency call service, playing a significant role in combating crime, maintaining public security, and serving the community. During his tenure in Fujian, Xi visited the police unit three times to inspect and guide its work. Recently, members of the unit wrote to Xi, reporting on their work and expressing their determination to fulfill duties on the new journey.

item.title: China opposes any official engagements between its diplomatic partners and Taiwan authorities: FM
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- China firmly opposes official interactions and engagements of any form between the Taiwan authorities and countries having diplomatic ties with China, and does not allow interference in its internal affairs by any external forces, foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday. Guo made the remarks at a regular press briefing in response to a media report that some Panamanian lawmakers recently set up a so-called "Panama-Taiwan parliamentary exchange group" and U.S. lawmakers attended the launch of the group via video link. According to the report, Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino reiterated that "foreign relations are directed by the Executive," and that parliamentarians' engagements with Taiwan "does not mean that the Executive endorses them." There is but one China in the world and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory, Guo said. "We urge those few politicians to see the real picture. To cross the line on the Taiwan question will lead to serious consequences," he said. The establishment of this so-called "parliamentary exchange group" seriously violates the one-China principle upheld by Panama, the spokesperson said. "We noted the statement of the Panamanian government and hope that Panama will honor its commitment to the one-China principle with real actions to uphold the political foundation of China-Panama relations," Guo said. China urges the United States to abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiques, stop sending the wrong message to "Taiwan independence" separatist forces, and stop disrupting and sabotaging China-Panama relations, the spokesperson said.

item.title: Chinese defense minister holds talks with Lao deputy prime minister and defense minister
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Defense Minister Dong Jun held talks with visiting Lao Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense Khamlieng Outhakaysone in Beijing on Monday. Dong said the Chinese military is ready to work with the Lao military to further strengthen high-level exchanges, enhance the quality and efficiency of practical cooperation in various fields, provide strong support for building an all-weather China-Laos community with a shared future in the new era, and safeguard regional stability. Khamlieng Outhakaysone said the Lao side is willing to strengthen high-level communication and exchanges at various levels between the two militaries, and promote practical cooperation across various fields to achieve more outcomes. This year marks the 65th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Laos. Since Sept. 7, the Chinese and Lao militaries have been conducting a joint military exercise in Vientiane, Laos, codenamed "Peace Train-2026," focusing on humanitarian assistance and medical services. The exercise is scheduled to run through late September, making it the sixth joint exercise of its kind between the two militaries since 2017.

item.title: Fueling Japan's neo-militarism will push region toward dangerous vortex: Chinese spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese defense spokesperson on Monday voiced firm opposition to a joint military exercise by Japan, the United States and Australia, warning that moves promoting Japan's military ambitions will drive the region into a perilous vortex. Jiang Bin, a spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defense, made the remarks at a press briefing when responding to a query concerning the "Orient Shield 26" exercise, which is being held in Japan from Sept. 8 to 24. This exercise is packaged as a "shield," but in reality it amounts to the forward deployment of strategic offensive weapons. It not only undermines other countries' legitimate security interests, but also heightens the risk of an arms race and military confrontation, and seriously threatens regional security and stability, Jiang said. Japan, as a defeated country of World War II, is prohibited from obtaining offensive weapons by the Potsdam Proclamation and Japan's pacifist constitution itself. However, in recent years, the country has continuously broken the constraints and its exclusively defense-oriented policy, vigorously developed long-range offensive weapons, and leveraged joint exercises with foreign countries to accelerate its "remilitarization," the spokesperson noted. "Any move that fuels Japan's military ambitions will only push the region into a dangerous vortex and will inevitably bring harm to those involved," Jiang warned. China urges relevant countries to respect other nations' security concerns, correct their wrong practices, and play a positive role in regional peace and stability with concrete actions, Jiang added.
